summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to Rs.107 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs.23 crore, with margin at 21.3% and a Rs.982 crore order book.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.107 crore, up 36% YoY, led by domestic facade (Rs.62 crore, +93%) and fenestration (Rs.6 crore, +127%), while international fell 12% to Rs.39 crore on delivery timing. EBITDA grew 9% to Rs.23 crore, and margin fell to 21.3% because of lower international contribution and a shift to DDP freight billing at cost. Management attributed about 1.5 points of the margin gap to freight pass-through and said the underlying margin is in line with FY26. PAT of Rs.17 crore grew more slowly than EBITDA due to lower other income (prior-year property sale gain) and higher depreciation from new capacity. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth, 23-25% EBITDA margin and 18-20% PAT margin, while flagging a weak first half and a heavier Q3 and Q4.

financial_highlights.change: Lower YoY; international margin cited at 36.3%
Grew slower than EBITDA; lower other income and higher depreciation

financial_highlights.metric: Freight cost included in revenue and cost
financial_highlights.change: Pass-through; adds about 1.5 pts to margin if excluded

segments.name: Domestic facade (turnkey, Grade A developers)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.62 crore, up 93% YoY; all order book is commercial real estate in Tier 1 cities. Historically about 49% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: International facade (B2B product supply, US and Australia)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.39 crore, down 12% YoY on delivery timing; management expects Q3 and Q4 to be stronger with three projects. Historically about 45% of FY26 revenue; FY26 Australia revenue was Rs.24 crore.

segments.name: Fenestration (luxury doors and windows)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs.6 crore, up 127% YoY on luxury residential demand. Historically about 6% of FY26 revenue. Higher margin, lower volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 25% YoY (management also cited a 20-25% CAGR ambition).
FY27 EBITDA margin of 23-25% and PAT margin of 18-20% on a consolidated basis, with freight pass-through expected to have limited impact.
Revenue mix for FY27 to stay similar to FY26 (about 49% domestic, 45% international, 6% fenestration).
Glass processing unit commissioning expected in about 8 months, with an estimated 1-1.5% EBITDA margin benefit.
Target of at least 2 years of order book visibility.
capex_capacity: Vile Bhagad (Mangaon) plant on a 1 lakh sq m owned MIDC plot; about 32,000 sq m built to date and about 30% of land used.
Current capacity about 130 panels a day across four production lines, with about 350 workers (about 120 on payroll).
Glass processing unit under construction; total project cost Rs.80 crore, funded by Rs.50 crore fresh issue and internal accruals; commissioning in about 8 months.
Management says infrastructure supports growth for the next couple of years without incremental capex.
In-house NABL-accredited test facility for air, water, seismic, structural and movement testing.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs.982 crore as on 31 July 2026, with no substantial new orders in the past three months; a few near-closure international jobs in the US, Canada and Israel.
Domestic facade market about Rs.9,000 crore, projected to reach about Rs.14,500 crore by FY30 (about 15.9% CAGR, per management).
Management estimates a 6-7% domestic market share, and says it is the second-largest domestic player by revenue.
Contracts include aluminium and glass pass-through across all verticals; freight now billed at cost under DDP terms.
Payment terms are milestone-based (about 10% advance, about 55-60% on material delivery, balance on installation); export invoicing is at dispatch with 60-day credit.
Management said US tariffs could slow US construction demand, but it views the impact on its business as small.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q1 order inflow, and will the freight change and any Q1 delays affect Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no substantial new order came in over the past three months. Freight of about Rs.5.5 crore is a pass-through, and adjusting for it plus the prior-year property gain, margin is in line with FY26. Export is back-ended, with three projects due in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin risen above pre-COVID levels on lower revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the export and fenestration verticals, a shift from residential to commercial projects with faster realisations, pass-through clauses on aluminium and glass, and consolidation from three factories to one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the glass processing unit timeline and benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is expected in about 8 months, with an estimated 1-1.5% bottom-line margin benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order-book and growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to keep at least 2 years of visibility and grow revenue at 20-25% CAGR; a typical order cycle is 18-24 months (export about 12 months, domestic about 24).

qa_highlights.question: What are the market share and competitive position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates about 6-7% domestic share and says it is second-largest by revenue; its direct competitors are three or four players with revenue around Rs.200 crore.

risks_watch: Seasonality: management said the first two quarters are typically slow, so FY27 delivery depends on the heavier Q3 and Q4.
Order inflow: no substantial new orders in the three months to July, and the company is relying on near-closure international wins.
Freight and duty pass-through: under DDP terms the company bears freight and any tariff changes, and mitigation depends on clients accepting pass-through; management said margin % may dilute.
US demand: management said tariffs could slow US construction demand.
Glass processing unit commissioning in about 8 months; the margin benefit is estimated at 1-1.5%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margin and FY27 guidance, which management reiterated despite the quarter's margin dip. Somewhat evasive on order inflow, export margin split and forward mix, and it repeatedly asked investors to judge on a yearly basis rather than quarterly.
key_quotes: So the margin hasn't deteriorated at all to that extent. It is at par with what we have delivered over the last financial year and what we are committing to deliver this year.
I encourage all the investors today on call to look at this business from a long -term perspective at a yearly level, as opposed to quarterly levels
